title: Matrix shading ignores large shifts that are negative or unattributed
description: On two-axis dimension pages (e.g. /religion-v2/, 'Every religion, every task'), site/src/components/Matrix.astro shades only cells whose interval lies ABOVE the floor ('detected'). Cells whose interval lies below the floor ('reverse of the trope') and cells marked 'unattributed' render white regardless of size, so large shifts look like no bias. The leaderboard counts bias in either direction, so shading must follow the size of the shift whenever its interval excludes the floor, in either direction, with direction shown by sign and a non-colour cue. Unattributed cells need their own clearly explained style, not white. The pre-registered outline also goes (results-first story BD-e84479). Reported by the author 2026-09-23.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Feature: Matrix shading follows the size of the bias
  Scenario: A large shift below the floor is shaded
    Given a cell whose interval lies entirely below the floor
    When the matrix is built
    Then the cell is shaded by the absolute size of the shift on the same scale as cells above the floor, and marked as reverse direction by sign and a pattern or icon
  Scenario: Only cells whose interval includes the floor are unshaded
    Given a cell whose interval includes the floor
    Then it is unshaded and labelled 'no bias detected at this floor'
  Scenario: Unattributed cells are explained
    Given a cell marked unattributed
    Then it has a distinct style and an accessible explanation, never plain white

comments.author: home
comments.text: 2026-09-23: fixed on main (Haiku pass A, reviewed by the coordinator): cells whose interval clears the floor in either direction are shaded by absolute size in alarm red; below-floor cells are striped; unattributed cells have a dashed outline; only no-bias cells stay plain. Checked on /stereotype-nationality/: American x worldliness -9.98 now shaded and striped.

right_now_summary: Matrix shading now highlights large shifts in either direction and gives unattributed cells a distinct style.
